# cantus

> A Python framework for writing LLM agent harnesses, designed for teaching on Google Colab and usable from any desktop with an API key. Students compose two protocol kinds (`Skill`, `Memory`), two hook helpers (`Analyzer`, `Validator`) and five `cantus.workflows` building blocks over either a local Gemma 4 model or a cloud `ChatModel`. This file is a single-shot context for *external* LLMs (Claude, GPT, Gemini, NotebookLM) so they can produce framework-style code on request.

## Versioning

- Current release: `v0.5.0` (PyPI name `cantus-agent`, import name `cantus`). Install with `pip install cantus-agent==0.5.0`; add extras as needed: `cantus-agent[runtime]` (local Gemma 4 loader), `cantus-agent[providers]` (openai + anthropic + google + groq), `cantus-agent[serve]` (FastAPI server + channels), `cantus-agent[tui]` (terminal dashboard).
- Git install: `pip install git+https://github.com/schola-cantorum/cantus@v0.5.0`.
- Notebooks: open `notebooks/task_template.ipynb` in Colab via `https://colab.research.google.com/github/schola-cantorum/cantus/blob/v0.5.0/notebooks/task_template.ipynb`. The companion `notebooks/admin_setup.ipynb` mirrors Gemma 4 weights to Drive once per installation.

## When to use this file

Paste this whole file into a fresh chat with an external LLM, then ask it to write a new `@skill`, an `@analyzer` / `@validator` hook, a `Memory` subclass, or a `cantus.workflows` composition. The output should `ast.parse` cleanly, use the right decorator and signature shape, and follow the docstring convention below.

## Public API surface

```python
from cantus import (
    # Decorator entries (most common)
    skill, debug,
    # Function-pass entry
    register_skill,
    # Class-first base classes
    Skill, Memory,
    # Memory implementations (class-only)
    ShortTermMemory, BM25Memory, EmbeddingMemory, MarkdownMemory, AutoMemory,
    # Identity
    Soul, SoulParseError,
    # Runtime
    Action, CallSkillAction, FinalAnswerAction,
    Observation, SkillObservation, ToolErrorObservation,
    ValidationErrorObservation, MaxIterationsObservation,
    EventStream, JsonLinesPersistence, Agent, AgentState, Inspector,
    Registry, get_registry, Result,
    # Tier 2 chat models (cloud / local servers)
    ChatModel, Message, ToolCall, ChatResponse, ChatModelAsHandle, load_chat_model,
    # Environment profiles
    ColabEnvironment, LocalEnvironment, CloudOnlyEnvironment,
    # Tier 1 local Gemma loader (not in __all__, but importable)
    mount_drive_and_load,
)
from cantus.hooks import analyzer, validator, Analyzer, Validator   # hook helpers
from cantus.workflows import PromptChain, Router, Parallel, OrchestratorWorker, EvaluatorOptimizer
```

Things that do **not** exist (do not generate them): `@memory`, `register_memory`, `@workflow`, `register_workflow`, `Workflow`, a top-level `analyzer` / `validator` import, and `state.final_answer`. Memory needs state, so it is a class. Analyzer and Validator are hook helpers imported from `cantus.hooks`; they attach to a Skill and are never registered on their own. Workflows are plain classes in `cantus.workflows`.

## Skill — a tool the LLM can call

```python
from cantus import skill

@skill
def search_book(title: str, lang: str = "zh-TW") -> str:
    """Search the library catalog.

    Args:
        title: book title keyword.
        lang: locale hint, default zh-TW.

    Returns:
        A string with one line per match.
    """
    ...
```

The signature becomes the Pydantic args schema. The first paragraph of the docstring becomes the LLM-facing description. The `Args:` block becomes per-arg descriptions. `@skill` registers the function into the process-wide `Registry` under kind `"skill"`, the only registry kind.

Function-pass form: `register_skill(search_book)`.
Class-first form:

```python
from cantus import Skill

class SearchBook(Skill):
    """Search the library catalog."""
    name = "search_book"
    def run(self, title: str, lang: str = "zh-TW") -> str: ...
```

## Analyzer and Validator — hooks attached to a Skill

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from cantus import skill
from cantus.hooks import analyzer, validator, Result

class Book(BaseModel):
    title: str
    isbn: str

@analyzer
def parse_query(text: str) -> dict:
    """Normalise the raw query before the skill runs."""
    return {"title": text.strip()}

@validator
def ensure_isbn_valid(result: str) -> Result:
    """Reject results whose ISBN-13 checksum fails."""
    if checksum_ok(result):
        return Result.success(result)
    return Result.failure(f"ISBN checksum mismatch in {result}")

@skill(pre_hook=parse_query, post_hook=ensure_isbn_valid)
def search_book(title: str) -> str:
    """Search the library catalog."""
    ...
```

The agent runs `pre_hook(**args)` before the skill and `post_hook(result)` after it. A `post_hook` returning `Result(ok=False, ...)` becomes a `ValidationErrorObservation`; the loop shows the feedback to the LLM and retries up to `max_retries` (default 3). A validator must always return `Result.success(...)` or `Result.failure(...)`. The names `non_empty_final_answer` and `action_parse` are reserved for the framework's own validators.

## Workflows — five plain-Python building blocks

```python
from cantus.workflows import PromptChain, Router, Parallel, OrchestratorWorker, EvaluatorOptimizer

pipeline = PromptChain(steps=[search_book, parse_book_list, pick_top_three])
books = pipeline.run("sci-fi")
```

Each class takes registered `Skill` instances (or any callable) in its constructor and exposes `.run(input) -> output`. `Router(routes, classifier)` picks a branch; `Parallel(branches)` runs every branch (sequentially, in-process) and returns the list; `OrchestratorWorker(orchestrator, workers)` hands sub-tasks to workers round-robin; `EvaluatorOptimizer(generator, evaluator, max_iters=3)` loops until the evaluator accepts. Workflows never register themselves and never appear in the registry's LLM-facing spec.

## Memory — class-only, five built-in implementations

```python
from cantus import Memory
from cantus.protocols.memory import Turn

class TopicMemory(Memory):
    """Remember topics the student has asked about."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.topics: list[str] = []

    def remember(self, turn: Turn) -> None:
        self.topics.append(turn.user)

    def recall(self, query: str) -> list[Turn]:
        return [Turn(user=t, assistant="") for t in self.topics if query in t]
```

Built-in implementations:

- `ShortTermMemory(n=10)` — most recent N turns (`collections.deque`)
- `BM25Memory(top_k=5)` — keyword retrieval (requires `cantus-agent[memory]`)
- `EmbeddingMemory(top_k=5)` — semantic retrieval (requires `cantus-agent[memory]`)
- `MarkdownMemory(path)` — turns persisted as Markdown chunks on disk
- `AutoMemory(backend)` — wraps any `Memory` and exposes `view` / `create` / `str_replace` / `delete` Skills so the LLM edits its own memory

## Tool-call grammar (for reference)

The agent asks the LLM for exactly one JSON object per turn:

```json
{
  "thought": "<free-form reasoning text>",
  "action": {"skill_name": "<one-of-registered>", "args": {...}}
}
```

or, to terminate:

```json
{
  "thought": "<free-form>",
  "action": {"final_answer": "<string>"}
}
```

`skill_name` must be a registered skill and `args` must satisfy that skill's Pydantic schema; anything else is recorded as a `ValidationErrorObservation` and retried. `thought` is free text.

## Running an agent

```python
from cantus import Agent, ChatModelAsHandle, load_chat_model, mount_drive_and_load

# Tier 1: local Gemma 4 on Colab (requires cantus-agent[runtime])
model = mount_drive_and_load(variant="E4B")          # or "E2B"
agent = Agent(model=model)

# Tier 2: any cloud / local-server provider — MUST be wrapped in ChatModelAsHandle
chat = load_chat_model("openai/gpt-4o-mini")          # reads OPENAI_API_KEY
agent = Agent(model=ChatModelAsHandle(chat, system="You are terse."))

state = agent.run("Recommend three sci-fi books", max_iterations=8)
final = state.stream[-1]                               # FinalAnswerAction when converged
print(getattr(final, "answer", final))
```

`agent.run(query)` returns an `AgentState` with `.query` and `.stream` (an `EventStream` of `Action` / `Observation` objects). There is no `final_answer` attribute on the state; the answer is `stream[-1].answer` when the last event is a `FinalAnswerAction`. If the loop hits `max_iterations`, the last event is a `MaxIterationsObservation` instead. `Inspector(state.stream).replay()` prints the full trace. Provider prefixes: `openai/`, `anthropic/`, `google/`, `groq/`, `nvidia/`, `ollama/`, `omlx/`, `mlx/` (the last three need no API key).

## Serving skills over HTTP (optional, requires cantus-agent[serve])

```python
from cantus.serve import serve
from cantus import get_registry
import uvicorn

app = serve(get_registry())          # each skill -> POST /skills/<name>; GET /health, /skills, /introspection
uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=8765)
```

Or from the shell: `cantus serve --registry-import my_module:registry`, then `cantus tui` for the read-only terminal dashboard.

## Common patterns

```python
# @debug stacking — opt-in trace of a Skill / Analyzer / Validator instance
from cantus import debug, skill
@debug
@skill
def traced_search(title: str) -> str: ...
# stdout will include: [debug] traced_search args=... result=...

# Give the agent a personality from a SOUL.md file
from cantus import Agent, Soul
agent = Agent(model=model, soul=Soul.from_file("SOUL.md"))
```

## Style rules for generated code

- Always use type annotations on every parameter and return.
- Always include a Google-style docstring with description and `Args:` block.
- Decorator goes on the line *immediately above* the function definition.
- Stack `@debug` *above* `@skill`, never below.
- Hooks attach through `@skill(pre_hook=..., post_hook=...)`; never register an analyzer or validator on its own.
- For validators, always return `Result.success(...)` or `Result.failure(...)`.
- Memory subclasses always implement both `recall(query)` and `remember(turn)`.
- Wrap any `ChatModel` in `ChatModelAsHandle` before giving it to `Agent`.
